skill.name: curlshot
skill.description: Take screenshots of web pages with the CurlShot API. Use when the user wants a screenshot, full-page capture, mobile or tablet view, PDF, or scrolling video of a URL, or wants their own HTML or Markdown rendered to an image or PDF. Needs a CurlShot access key in the CURLSHOT_API_KEY environment variable.
skill.summary: Capture public web pages or render supplied HTML and Markdown through the hosted CurlShot API.
skill.author: sergiupogor

security_audit.summary: All 35 static matches concern Markdown formatting, documented service endpoints, intended authentication, or remote webpage rendering rather than desktop surveillance. No evidence found of malicious exfiltration or prompt injection. The local-page workaround lacks a consent and redaction check before sending potentially private HTML to CurlShot.

remediation.issue: The local-page workaround recommends exporting HTML without checking whether external processing is authorized.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before uploading local or private content, remove secrets and personal data, and offer local rendering when external processing is prohibited.

remediation.issue: The setup guidance asks the user for a missing API key without specifying a secure configuration channel.
remediation.suggestion: Ask users to configure CURLSHOT_API_KEY through their environment or secret manager rather than pasting credentials into the conversation.

semantic_findings.title: Private HTML export lacks a consent safeguard
semantic_findings.description: The workaround says "for a local page, send its HTML instead" and supplies an external POST workflow. No approval or redaction step protects private content before export.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The local-page workaround and hosted upload are explicit, but no privacy check is specified. This creates an accidental disclosure risk, not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Creating consistent web captures across devices and formats requires repeated setup. This skill guides Claude and Codex through CurlShot requests for screenshots, PDFs, and scrolling videos.
actual_capabilities: Request webpage images in PNG, JPEG, or WebP, with full-page or CSS-selector captures.
Configure device presets, viewport dimensions, pixel density, and dark mode.
Render supplied HTML or Markdown into images or PDFs through authenticated POST requests.
Request scrolling page captures in MP4, WebM, or GIF.
Configure loading waits, delays, banner blocking, ad blocking, and cached results.
Describe the hosted MCP alternative with take_screenshot and list_devices tools.
limitations: Rendering requires a CurlShot account, an API key, network access, and available service quota.
Localhost and private network addresses are refused; supplied HTML is processed externally instead.
The package contains instructions only, not a local browser renderer or a tested service implementation.
Authenticated private-page workflows, service retention policies, and output quality guarantees are not documented in this skill.

best_practices: Configure CURLSHOT_API_KEY securely and keep it out of chat, repository files, and displayed links.
Obtain approval for external processing and remove sensitive data before submitting local HTML or Markdown.
Encode target URLs, verify HTTP status, and choose explicit output formats and viewport settings.
anti_patterns: Sending confidential local content to CurlShot without authorization.
Treating an error response saved with an image extension as a successful capture.
Assuming localhost or private network URLs are reachable by the hosted renderer.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure CURLSHOT_API_KEY for HTTP requests. The documented MCP alternative uses bearer authentication.

faq.question: Can I capture a local development server?
faq.answer: Localhost and private network addresses are refused. You can submit approved HTML instead, but CurlShot processes that content externally.

faq.question: Which output formats are documented?
faq.answer: The skill lists PNG, JPEG, WebP, PDF, MP4, WebM, and GIF. Video formats represent scrolling page captures.

faq.question: Can I render Markdown directly?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented POST workflow accepts a Markdown field instead of HTML and supports image or PDF output.

faq.question: Can I use MCP instead of curl?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents a hosted MCP endpoint with take_screenshot and list_devices tools. Client setup is referenced but not included.

faq.question: How is usage counted?
faq.answer: The skill states that successful renders count toward usage, while failed renders and cache hits are free. Confirm current terms with CurlShot.
